QUIC means version 1 unless a relation says otherwise; RFC 9002's example controller is not the only permitted congestion controller.
Worked numbers describe constructed cases, not measured browser or network performance.
Server-push disablement is bounded to Chrome 106's announced default HTTP/2 behavior; push remains described by the HTTP/2 and HTTP/3 standards.
scope: HTTP/1.1 (RFC 9112), HTTP/2 (RFC 9113/7541), HTTP/3 (RFC 9114/9204), QUIC v1 (RFC 9000/9001/9002), TLS 1.3 early data, and Chrome 106's default HTTP/2 push disablement; later QUIC extensions, universal browser policy, and application-specific performance guarantees are excluded.
statement: A path policy that prevents the UDP datagrams needed by a selected QUIC endpoint from reaching the peer.
